stories.h: Alaafin of Oyo says he is the foremost traditional ruler in Yorubaland
stories.p: The Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Owoade I, has said history makes him the number one traditional ruler in Yorubaland, while insisting he is not competing with the Ooni of Ife. The two stools clashed last year over a chieftaincy title.
body: The Alaafin of Oyo, Oba Abimbola Akeem Owoade I, has described himself as the foremost traditional ruler in Yorubaland.
## What he said

In a television interview reported on Friday, 6 November 2026, the monarch said that, going by history and the contribution of the old Oyo Empire to Yoruba civilisation, the Alaafin is number one. He denied that he was in a contest for supremacy with any other Yoruba ruler, including the Ooni of Ife, Oba Enitan Ogunwusi. He said he regularly prays for the progress of the Yoruba people and believes that when Oyo succeeds, all Yoruba people are honoured.
## The earlier dispute

His comments follow a dispute between the two thrones in August 2025, after the Ooni conferred the title of Okanlomo of Yorubaland on Ibadan businessman Dotun Sanusi. The Alaafin gave the Ooni 48 hours to withdraw the title, arguing that the Ooni's authority was limited to a few local government areas in Osun State and that the title was unlawful. The Ooni's spokesman later said the monarch had told him not to respond to what he called an empty threat.
## Background

The question of which monarch ranks highest in Yorubaland has been debated for many years. The Alaafin's supporters point to the power of the old Oyo Empire, while the Ooni's supporters point to Ile-Ife's place as the traditional cradle of the Yoruba people. Oba Owoade was crowned Alaafin in 2025, succeeding the late Oba Lamidi Adeyemi III.
more: The Alaafin says history makes him number one.
He says he is not competing with the Ooni.
The two thrones clashed over a title in 2025.

stories.h: California governor Gavin Newsom commutes all 548 death sentences
stories.p: California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 people on the state's death row to life in prison without parole, saying the state cannot morally kill them. California has not carried out an execution in about two decades.
body: California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted every death sentence in the state to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole.
## What he announced

In an official letter on Thursday, 5 November 2026, Newsom said the decision affects 548 people on death row, one of the largest death row populations in the world. He said he was acting on a long-held belief that society is stronger when it rejects state-sanctioned killing. He acknowledged that many Californians believe people who commit brutal crimes deserve to die, but said he had concluded that the state cannot morally kill them.
## Why all at once

Newsom said he chose a blanket commutation rather than reviewing cases one by one because trying to separate crimes and offenders would create two classes of murder victims. He said the offenders would now spend the rest of their lives in prison, and that he hoped the move would separate the memory of victims from the fate of those who harmed them.
## Background

California has not carried out an execution in about two decades, although courts continued to hand down death sentences. In 2019, Newsom placed a moratorium on executions and closed the state's execution chamber. Newsom, a Democrat, is in the final months of his second term as governor and is widely seen as a possible future presidential candidate. The decision comes days after the Democrats' strong performance in the US midterm elections.
California voters rejected ballot measures to abolish the death penalty in 2012 and 2016, and Newsom's decision is likely to face criticism from supporters of capital punishment.
more: 548 death sentences were commuted to life without parole.
Newsom said the state cannot morally kill offenders.
California has not executed anyone in about 20 years.

stories.h: Three dead, 14 in hospital after drinking herbal mixtures in Benue
stories.p: At least three people have reportedly died and 14 others are receiving treatment after drinking herbal mixtures sold by hawkers in Oju Local Government Area of Benue State. The local government chairman says suspects have been arrested.
body: At least three people have reportedly died and 14 others have been taken to hospital after drinking herbal mixtures suspected to contain harmful substances in Benue State.
## What happened

According to reports on Friday, 6 November 2026, three men hawking the herbal preparations sold them to residents during a market day in Oju Township, Oju Local Government Area, last weekend. A resident said panic broke out on Monday, 2 November, when several people who had taken the mixtures began showing similar symptoms. One person died on Tuesday, a second early on Wednesday and a third on Thursday. Fourteen others are being treated at the General Hospital in Oju, four of them reportedly in a critical condition.
## Suspects arrested

The chairman of Oju Local Government Area, Jackson Ominyi, confirmed the incident and said the suspected sellers had been arrested and taken to the state police headquarters in Makurdi. He said three deaths had been recorded as of Thursday, but that he did not yet have a final figure. The suspects have not been charged in court, and the substances in the mixtures have not been officially identified.
## Background

Unregulated herbal mixtures are widely sold in markets and on the streets across Nigeria, often with claims that they cure many illnesses. Health authorities, including the food and drug regulator NAFDAC, have repeatedly warned Nigerians against buying unregistered medicines from hawkers.
## What happens next
Residents are urging the authorities to investigate and to stop the sale of unregulated herbal products in the area.
more: Three people have reportedly died.
Fourteen others are in hospital, four critically.
The suspected sellers have been arrested.

stories.h: Tinubu approves Ibom Deep Seaport request during Akwa Ibom campaign, promises jobs and economic development
stories.p: At his campaign rally in Uyo, President Bola Tinubu announced on the spot that he had approved a request from Akwa Ibom's leadership for international export status for the Ibom Deep Seaport. He also promised jobs, skills development and investment in the state's palm economy.
body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has approved a request linked to the long-awaited Ibom Deep Seaport, announcing the decision while addressing supporters at his presidential campaign rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.
## "I look, and I approve it"
Speaking from the podium, flanked by party leaders and security officials, Tinubu told the crowd that the state's leadership had brought a request to him.
"Now your leader makes a request, for international export status. I look, and I approve it," he said, to cheers from supporters.
The Ibom Deep Seaport has been one of Akwa Ibom's biggest ambitions for years, with successive state governments pushing for it as a way to open the state to international trade and create jobs.
## Promises of jobs and skills
Tinubu also used the occasion to make several promises about the state's economic future.
"I promise you skill development. I promise you jobs," he said. "We are going to plant a lot of economic trees."

He pointed to the palm tree, a major part of the region's economy, as an opportunity. "There is no reason why we cannot use the value of palm trees and the palm here," he said, adding that there was no reason the country could not create skills development that is "everlasting".
## "Development must be even"
The President said growth must reach every part of the country. "Development must be even, inclusive and reasonable. It must bring progress and create economic value," he said.
## What it means
If the approval leads to real progress on the seaport, it could be a major boost for Akwa Ibom's economy, bringing shipping, logistics and related businesses to the state.
But campaign promises are easy to make at rallies. Nigerians will be watching to see whether the approval is followed by funding, construction and the jobs that have been promised.
## Over to you
Is Tinubu's approval of the Ibom Deep Seaport request a genuine step forward for Akwa Ibom, or just another campaign promise ahead of 2027?
more: Tinubu said he approved international export status at the rally.
He promised jobs and skills development.
He highlighted the value of Akwa Ibom's palm economy.

stories.h: Lagos Trade Fair erupts as Peter Obi attends funeral of popular market leader Chief Okey Ezibe (Omeluora)
stories.p: Peter Obi drew a huge, cheering crowd at the Trade Fair International Market in Lagos as he came to pay his last respects to the late Chief Sir Okey Ezibe, popularly known as Omeluora, regarded as one of the founding fathers of Balogun Market.
body: It was an emotional scene at the Trade Fair International Market in Lagos as former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, the NDC presidential candidate and Labour Party candidate in the 2023 election, arrived to pay his last respects to the late Chief Sir Okey Ezibe, popularly known as Omeluora.

Chief Ezibe, widely regarded as one of the founding fathers of the famous Balogun Market in Lagos, was honoured by traders, associates, friends and well-wishers who gathered to celebrate his life and his contribution to commerce.
## "My leader! My leader!"

Something remarkable happened when Obi arrived. The atmosphere suddenly changed. Traders stepped away from their businesses, and a large crowd gathered around him, cheering and calling out, "My leader! My leader!"
Many raised their phones to capture the moment, while members of his team, wearing T-shirts printed with "Rest in Peace Omeluora", waved to the crowd from his car.

For those watching, the reception was another reminder of the strong support Obi continues to enjoy among sections of the trading community, particularly in Lagos. He had come for a solemn occasion, yet his presence drew the kind of attention usually seen at major political gatherings.
## Who was Chief Okey Ezibe (Omeluora)?

To many traders, the late Chief Sir Okey Ezibe was more than a successful businessman. He was a respected figure whose contributions helped shape the business community around Balogun Market, one of Nigeria's busiest commercial centres.

For years, Balogun Market has provided opportunities for thousands of traders, importers, wholesalers and small business owners. People like Omeluora are remembered for building business networks, encouraging younger entrepreneurs and strengthening the trading community. His passing marks the loss of a respected figure in that community.
## Obi's reception gets people talking

Despite the disagreements and controversies that surround Nigerian politics, Obi still draws enthusiastic crowds in parts of the country, and the scenes at Trade Fair appeared to reflect that connection.

Some will see the reception as a sign of his political popularity ahead of the 2027 general election. Others may simply see it as a warm welcome for a familiar public figure attending the funeral of a respected businessman.
Whatever the interpretation, the excitement around his arrival became one of the memorable moments of the day.
## Remembering Omeluora
Beyond the cheers and the political talk, the gathering was ultimately about remembering Chief Okey Ezibe and the legacy he left behind.

A man can build wealth, businesses and influence in his lifetime, but what people say about him after his death often tells another story. For Omeluora, the respect shown by the trading community speaks to the place he held in their lives.
Rest in peace, Omeluora. A great iroko has fallen. His name will continue to be remembered among those who helped commerce grow in Lagos.
## Over to you
Is the reception Peter Obi received at Lagos Trade Fair another sign of his political strength ahead of 2027, or was it simply a show of respect from traders? Share your thoughts.
more: Obi attended the funeral of Chief Okey Ezibe (Omeluora) at Trade Fair.
Omeluora is regarded as a founding father of Balogun Market.
Traders mobbed Obi, chanting 'My leader!'

stories.h: Shettima says Peter Obi has run himself out of the 2027 race
stories.p: Vice-President Kashim Shettima told an APC rally in Uyo that NDC candidate Peter Obi had destroyed his own chances in 2027, mocking his comparisons with Bangladesh. The rally followed President Tinubu's inauguration of projects in Akwa Ibom.
body: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has said that Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), has ruined his own chances in the 2027 election.
## What he said

Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on Friday, 6 November 2026, Shettima reportedly said Obi had run himself out of the race through what he called lies and bogus statistics. He suggested that Obi had recently travelled abroad quietly before returning to Nigeria, and that he had thrown away the goodwill he once enjoyed among voters. The vice-president also mocked Obi's frequent comparisons between Nigeria and Bangladesh, saying a shirt made for one country cannot fit another, and dismissed Obi's claim that he won the 2023 presidential election.
## Tinubu in Akwa Ibom

Before the rally, President Bola Tinubu inaugurated several projects built by Governor Umo Eno's administration, including the new terminal building at Victor Attah International Airport in Uyo. Tinubu described the visit as a homecoming, praised Eno as a visionary leader, and said the airport's international flight status was the result of the governor's commitment to the state. The President also took a swipe at Obi at the event over erosion in Anambra State.
## Background

Obi, a former Anambra governor, came third in the 2023 presidential election and challenged the result in court, insisting he won. He is running again in 2027 with Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate. The presidential election is scheduled for 16 January 2027. Obi's campaign had not publicly responded to Shettima's remarks at the time of writing.
more: Shettima spoke at an APC rally in Uyo.
He mocked Obi's comparisons with Bangladesh.
Tinubu inaugurated a new airport terminal in Uyo.

stories.h: INEC warns of plot to threaten and kidnap election workers ahead of 2027
stories.p: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan says intelligence operations with the DSS uncovered a plot to intimidate and abduct ad hoc election staff, and that suspects have been arrested and charged. He warned officials against bias and negligence.
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned of an alleged plot to threaten, intimidate and abduct temporary election workers ahead of the 2027 general elections.
## What INEC said

Speaking in Lokoja, Kogi State, on Friday, 6 November 2026, during a North Central zonal readiness assessment, INEC chairman Professor Joash Amupitan said intelligence-led operations carried out with the Department of State Services (DSS) had led to the arrest of key suspects, who have since been charged in court. He warned that anyone who interferes with or harms election workers will be prosecuted to the full extent of the law. He did not give details of the suspects or the charges.
## Warning to staff

Amupitan also warned electoral officers against negligence and political bias, saying neutrality at local level would directly affect public trust in the elections. He said credible elections cannot be achieved through last-minute arrangements, and that INEC is working with security agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security to tackle threats early.
## Background

INEC expects to manage more than 103 million registered voters across 176,846 polling units in 2027. The commission relies on hundreds of thousands of ad hoc staff, many of them members of the National Youth Service Corps, to run polling units, and attacks on election workers and offices have been a concern in past elections. This week INEC has also faced questions about about 1.5 million questionable entries found in the voter register, and disowned a fake poster about the ADC's leadership.
## What happens next
The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for 16 January 2027.
more: INEC says suspects have been arrested and charged.
Amupitan warned officials against political bias.
More than 103 million voters are expected to be registered.

stories.h: Nigeria's external debt rises to $145 billion, World Bank report says
stories.p: Nigeria's external debt rose 6.6% to about $145 billion in 2025, according to the World Bank's latest International Debt Report. Some debt ratios improved, but repayments took a bigger share of export earnings.
body: Nigeria's external debt reached about $145.0 billion in 2025, according to the World Bank's International Debt Report 2026.
## The figures

According to reports on Friday, 6 November 2026, the total was 6.6 per cent higher than the year before and about 74 per cent higher than the $83.2 billion recorded in 2015. Public and publicly guaranteed debt made up about $62.4 billion of the total, private debt without government guarantees about $54.5 billion, and short-term debt about $28.1 billion. Multilateral lenders were the biggest creditors of the government, at about $31.4 billion, including about $18.5 billion owed to the World Bank's International Development Association. China remained Nigeria's largest single-country lender, owed about $5.7 billion.
## Burden of repayments

Some measures of the debt burden improved: external debt fell to 212 per cent of export earnings and to 51 per cent of gross national income. But debt service took a bigger share of income, rising to 19 per cent of exports and 5 per cent of gross national income.
## The global picture

The World Bank said debt service payments by low- and middle-income countries reached $1.4 trillion in 2025, the fifth yearly rise in a row, driven largely by payments to private lenders such as bondholders. It noted that loans from official lenders carried an average interest rate of 1.9 per cent, compared with 9.6 per cent from private creditors.
## Why it matters

The figures come as President Bola Tinubu seeks Senate approval for new external borrowing of about $7.7 billion, a request opposition figures, including Atiku Abubakar, have urged lawmakers to reject. The government says borrowing is needed to fund infrastructure and that its reforms are improving the economy.
more: External debt rose 6.6% to about $145 billion.
China is the largest single-country lender.
Debt service took a bigger share of export earnings.

stories.h: Uzbekistan reportedly suspends visas and entry for Nigerians
stories.p: Uzbekistan has reportedly introduced temporary restrictions on issuing visas to Nigerians and on their entry into the country, according to a notice on an exhibition website. Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, Iraq and Bangladesh are said to be affected too.
body: Uzbekistan has reportedly introduced temporary restrictions on visas and entry for Nigerian citizens.
## What was announced

The restrictions came to light through a notice published on the website of the Green Energy Technologies Central Asia exhibition, reported on Friday, 6 November 2026. The notice said temporary restrictions had been introduced on issuing visas and on entry into Uzbekistan for citizens of the affected countries. It advised Nigerians who need to travel in exceptional circumstances to contact the consular section of the Uzbek embassy. Similar measures were reportedly listed for citizens of Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, Iraq and Bangladesh.
## No official explanation

Uzbekistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has not issued a public statement explaining the reasons for the restrictions or how long they will last, and its main visa portal does not mention them. The Nigerian government had not publicly reacted at the time of writing.
## Background

Uzbekistan, a former Soviet republic in Central Asia, has been trying to attract more tourists and investors in recent years. Nigerians already face strict visa requirements for many countries, and travel restrictions affecting Nigerian passport holders often spark debate at home about the country's image abroad.
## What it means for travellers
Nigerians planning trips to Uzbekistan, including for business events, are advised to check with the Uzbek embassy before making travel arrangements.
more: The notice appeared on an exhibition website.
Ghana, Kenya, Egypt, Iraq and Bangladesh are also listed.
Uzbekistan has not explained the move.

stories.h: Gunmen abduct 10 bus passengers on Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan road, demand ₦25m
stories.p: Gunmen have reportedly kidnapped 10 passengers travelling in a commercial bus on the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan road in Ogun State, including a recently discharged corps member. The kidnappers are said to be demanding ₦25 million.
body: Gunmen have reportedly abducted 10 passengers travelling on the Ijebu-Ode–Ibadan road in Ogun State and are demanding ₦25 million for their release.
## What happened

The passengers were travelling in a commercial bus when armed men stopped the vehicle shortly after it passed through Ijebu-Ode on Tuesday, 3 November 2026, and took them into a nearby forest, according to reports on Friday. Two recently discharged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) were said to be among the passengers; one escaped, while the other remains in captivity.
## Ransom demand

A relative of one of the victims said the incident was reported at a police station in Ijebu-Ode. She said the kidnappers later contacted the family using her brother's phone, first demanding ₦20 million and then raising it to ₦25 million. The Ogun State Police Command had not publicly commented at the time of writing.
## Background

Kidnapping on highways in the South-West has become a growing concern, with travellers on roads linking Ogun, Oyo and neighbouring states reporting attacks in recent years. Earlier this week, a court heard that suspects arrested over the abduction of corps members had admitted making confessional statements. Paying ransom is illegal in Nigeria, though families often say they feel they have no other choice.
## What happens next
Families of the victims are calling on the police and other security agencies to rescue the passengers.
more: Ten passengers were reportedly abducted on Tuesday.
A former corps member is among those held.
The kidnappers want ₦25 million.

stories.h: Troops rescue 16 kidnap victims in Niger State, recover weapons and cash
stories.p: The Nigerian Army says troops of 18 Brigade rescued 16 kidnapped people in an ambush in Kontagora LGA of Niger State, and recovered rifles, RPG bombs, 33 motorcycles and more than ₦4 million in cash.
body: The Nigerian Army says its troops have rescued 16 kidnapped people during operations against armed groups in Niger State.
## What the army said

In a statement on Friday, 6 November 2026, Captain Adebayo Samuel Adewumi of the army's 18 Brigade said the operations took place between 3 and 5 November. In the main operation on 5 November, troops acting on intelligence about armed men moving from Mashegu Local Government Area towards Rijiyan Nagwamatse in Kontagora Local Government Area set up an ambush. The army said it clashed with the group, which had abducted local residents, killed an unconfirmed number of the attackers and freed 16 victims.
## Items recovered

Troops said they recovered two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines, three rocket-propelled grenade bombs, 33 motorcycles, ammunition and about ₦4.1 million in cash. In a separate operation on 3 November, troops intercepted armed men moving from Kebbi State into Rijau Local Government Area of Niger State, forcing them to retreat, and recovered five motorcycles, a phone and about ₦644,000. The rescued victims received first aid and were handed over to the authorities to be reunited with their families.
## Background

Niger State has suffered repeated attacks and kidnappings by armed groups. Separately, the families of Islamiyya students abducted in Rafi Local Government Area last week say the kidnappers have demanded more than ₦100 million. The army did not say whether any of those students were among the people rescued.
## What happens next
The army said operations would continue across the state.
more: Sixteen kidnap victims were rescued.
Troops recovered rifles, RPG bombs and 33 motorcycles.
The operations took place in Kontagora and Rijau LGAs.

stories.h: Police Service Commission dismisses three senior officers, demotes 16 others
stories.p: The Police Service Commission has dismissed three senior police officers and demoted 16 others after misconduct investigations. It also reprimanded 23 officers, cleared three and reinstated some who had been suspended.
body: The Police Service Commission (PSC) has dismissed three senior police officers and demoted 16 others following investigations into misconduct.
## The decisions

In a statement reported on Friday, 6 November 2026, the commission's spokesman, Torty Kalu, said the decisions were made at a plenary session at its headquarters in Abuja on Tuesday, chaired by PSC chairman Hashimu Argungu, a retired deputy inspector-general of police. Besides the dismissals and demotions, 21 officers received severe reprimands and two received ordinary reprimands. Three officers were cleared of the allegations against them, and several officers who had been suspended were reinstated.
## Names not released

The commission did not name the officers or say what each had done. Argungu restated the commission's zero-tolerance stance on corruption, human rights abuses, interference in land and civil disputes, and other misconduct in the police.
## Background

The PSC is the body responsible for appointing, promoting and disciplining police officers, apart from the Inspector-General. Complaints of extortion, unlawful arrests and other abuses by police officers are common in Nigeria. This week, two officers were also detained in Nasarawa State over the alleged extortion of ₦150,000 from a traveller.
more: Three senior officers were dismissed.
Sixteen others were demoted.
The commission did not name the officers.

stories.h: Cute Abiola's old friend says the comedian drifted away after fame
stories.p: A TikToker who says he was once close to skit maker Cute Abiola has posted throwback videos complaining that their friendship faded after the comedian became successful. He insists it is not about money. Cute Abiola has not responded.
body: A TikToker who says he was once a close friend of skit maker The Cute Abiola has gone public with complaints that the comedian abandoned him after becoming famous.
## What he posted

The man, who goes by the handle Mayordona Nolan, posted a short clip on Wednesday, 4 November 2026, showing himself and Cute Abiola together in a car. He described the two of them and another friend as a close trio who supported each other through hard times, and said that two of them had since found success while he remained in a difficult situation, and the friendship had faded. He posted another throwback video of the three friends the next day.
## 'Not about money'
After some viewers accused him of feeling entitled, he posted a long clarification insisting that his posts had nothing to do with money or expectations of financial help.
## Background

Cute Abiola, a former member of the Nigerian Navy, is one of Nigeria's best-known skit makers. The complaints came in the same week that the comedian posted videos appealing to President Bola Tinubu over power cuts and economic hardship, saying he had sold one of his cars to settle debts.
## How people reacted

Reactions were divided. Some said friends who shared hard times should make an effort to stay in touch, while others said success does not create an obligation to keep every old relationship and accused the man of entitlement. Cute Abiola had not publicly responded at the time of writing.
more: The TikToker posted throwback videos with Cute Abiola.
He says the posts are not about money.
Cute Abiola has not responded.

stories.h: Tinubu takes swipe at Peter Obi in Akwa Ibom, says he confronted the Atlantic Ocean while Obi ran away from erosion in Anambra
stories.p: Speaking in Akwa Ibom, President Bola Tinubu accused NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi of failing to tackle erosion in Anambra State, while claiming he himself "tamed" the Atlantic Ocean, an apparent reference to the Eko Atlantic project in Lagos.
body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has taken a swipe at former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, comparing their records on tackling environmental challenges.
## What Tinubu said

Speaking in Akwa Ibom State, Tinubu accused Obi of failing to confront the serious erosion problems affecting Anambra State during his time as governor, and pointed out that Obi is now running for president under the NDC.

"Peter Obi is in one party they call NDC where he's running for president. He ran away from erosion in Anambra. He couldn't confront erosion. I, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, confronted the Atlantic Ocean. I tamed it for you," Tinubu said.
The President appeared to be referring to efforts to reclaim and protect land along the Lagos coastline, particularly the Eko Atlantic project, which began during his time as Lagos State governor.
## Can the two really be compared?

Anambra has struggled with severe gully erosion for decades, with communities losing farmland, roads and homes. Tackling it requires substantial funding, engineering work and cooperation between different levels of government.
The Eko Atlantic project, on the other hand, involved major private investment and extensive coastal engineering to reclaim land from the Atlantic Ocean.
Both involve serious environmental challenges, but their circumstances, funding arrangements and engineering requirements are quite different.
## The road to 2027
As the 2027 presidential election draws closer, exchanges like this are likely to become more common, with leaders publicly questioning one another's records in office.
Nigerians may also want to look closely at the actual results of these projects and the roles played by the leaders involved.
## Over to you

Does Tinubu's role in the Eko Atlantic project give him the right to question Peter Obi's record on erosion in Anambra State, or should Nigerians judge both men by their overall performance in public office?
more: Tinubu spoke at a campaign event in Akwa Ibom.
He said Obi 'ran away from erosion' in Anambra.
He appeared to refer to the Eko Atlantic project in Lagos.

stories.h: 2027: Atiku fires back at Tinubu, says he will be on the ballot and courts cannot stop Nigerians from deciding
stories.p: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has insisted he will contest the 2027 presidential election, reportedly telling President Tinubu that the courts cannot be used to escape the verdict of Nigerians. His message comes amid legal battles over his candidacy.
body: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has sent a pointed message to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, insisting he remains determined to contest the 2027 presidential election despite the legal and political battles surrounding the race.
In a statement attributed to him, Atiku reportedly declared that he is on the ballot and that the courts cannot be used to escape the verdict of Nigerians.
## A direct challenge
The message is a direct challenge to Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) as political activity builds ahead of the 2027 general elections.

It also raises a familiar question about the role of the judiciary in Nigeria's elections. Court judgments, disputes over party nominations and allegations of irregularities have shaped the country's politics for years.
## What is at stake

For President Tinubu, the next election will come amid continuing public debate over the cost of living, economic reforms and insecurity. Opposition politicians hope to turn those concerns into votes, while the government points to its reforms as long-term fixes.
For Atiku, getting onto the ballot will depend on party nomination processes, electoral requirements and the outcome of any legal decisions.
One thing is clear: the battle for 2027 is already taking shape, and more political confrontations are likely as the election draws closer.
## Over to you
If Atiku faces Tinubu again in 2027, do you think Nigerians will vote differently from how they voted in 2023? Or will the opposition need a completely different arrangement to win?
more: Atiku insists he will be on the 2027 presidential ballot.
He says courts cannot be used to escape the verdict of Nigerians.
His candidacy still faces legal and nomination hurdles.

stories.h: Imagine if Pastor Ibiyeomie's massive Hand of God Auditorium were a factory employing thousands of Nigerians
stories.p: Pastor David Ibiyeomie's huge Hand of God Auditorium has got people talking. But what if a structure of that size, and the money behind it, had been a factory creating thousands of jobs? A look at Nigeria's priorities.
body: When you look at the massive Hand of God Auditorium built by Pastor David Ibiyeomie, it is hard not to imagine something different.
What if a structure of that size, with all the money, planning, engineering and resources that went into it, were a massive factory producing goods for Nigerians and the international market?
## Imagine the jobs

Just imagine the number of young Nigerians who could be employed there: engineers, technicians, machine operators, electricians, cleaners, security staff, accountants, drivers and thousands of other workers earning salaries and caring for their families.
Think about the businesses that would spring up around it. Food vendors, transport operators, suppliers and small business owners would all benefit from the economic activity.

And imagine if that factory produced the things Nigeria currently spends billions importing. It could strengthen the economy, encourage local production and create opportunities for future generations.
## This is not an attack on the church

This is not an argument against Christianity, churches or places of worship. Everyone has the right to practise their religion, and religious organisations also provide jobs and contribute to society.
But Nigerians must begin to ask serious questions about our priorities as a nation.
## A nation searching for jobs

Millions of young Nigerians are searching for work. Many graduates have certificates but nowhere to work. Some have spent years learning skills, yet there are few industries where they can put those skills to use.
Meanwhile, the country keeps celebrating enormous buildings without giving the same attention to factories, industries and other investments that could provide lasting employment.
Imagine if wealthy Nigerians, including religious leaders, invested more heavily in manufacturing alongside their religious projects. Imagine the difference it could make.
## Prayer and production
A nation cannot pray its way into industrial development without also investing in production, skills, infrastructure and jobs.
Nigeria needs churches, yes. But it also desperately needs factories where young people can work, earn a decent living and build their future.
## Over to you
If you had the money to build an auditorium as big as Pastor Ibiyeomie's Hand of God, would you build a church, or a factory that could employ thousands of Nigerians?
more: Pastor David Ibiyeomie built the massive Hand of God Auditorium.
Could the same investment have created thousands of factory jobs?
Nigeria still imports billions in goods it could produce.

stories.h: FCCPC says some vegetable oils and salt in Nigerian markets fail nutrient standards
stories.p: The consumer protection agency FCCPC says 12% of vegetable oil samples and 2% of salt samples tested in markets and homes did not contain the nutrients required under Nigeria's food fortification rules. It has not named the brands.
body: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has raised concerns about the quality of some vegetable oils and salt sold in Nigeria, after tests found that some products did not meet national fortification standards.
## What the tests found

In a statement on Thursday, 5 November 2026, the commission's Director of Corporate Affairs, Ondaje Ijagwu, said the study was carried out over two months in randomly selected markets and households in northern and southern Nigeria, together with the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN). It examined 200 samples, made up of 100 vegetable oils and 100 salt products. According to the findings, 12 per cent of the vegetable oil samples and 2 per cent of the salt samples did not contain enough of the required nutrients. Of the oil samples, 49 were unbranded and 51 carried brand names, while 19 of the salt samples were unbranded and 81 were branded.
## Brands not named

The commission did not name the affected brands or say whether branded or unbranded products accounted for most of the failures. It said it had issued compliance directives to the manufacturers involved. The FCCPC also complained that few companies were using a digital tracking platform for fortified foods: only six vegetable oil makers had registered, and results for just eight of the 100 oil samples had been uploaded.
## What fortification means

Nigeria's fortification rules require some everyday foods to contain added vitamins and minerals, such as vitamin A in vegetable oil and iodine in salt, to help prevent nutritional deficiencies, especially among children and pregnant women. Products that fall short are not necessarily unsafe to eat, but they do not deliver the nutrients consumers are entitled to expect.
## What happens next
The commission said it would continue to monitor compliance. Consumers are advised to buy from trusted sources and check packaging and expiry dates.
more: 12% of vegetable oil samples failed the nutrient tests.
2% of salt samples also fell short.
The FCCPC has not named the brands.

stories.h: Doris Ogala reportedly taken to hospital after losing consciousness in detention
stories.p: Actress and Abia governorship candidate Doris Ogala has reportedly been taken to hospital after blacking out and bleeding while in detention, according to a video shared by a person close to her. Her bail ruling was due on Friday.
body: Nollywood actress Doris Ogala, the African Action Congress (AAC) governorship candidate in Abia State, has reportedly been taken to hospital from detention.
## What was said

On Thursday, 5 November 2026, a person close to the actress shared a video online saying he had spoken to her by phone while she was receiving treatment in hospital. According to him, she said she had lost consciousness, was bleeding and could not remember how she had been taken to the hospital. In the same video, Ogala could reportedly be heard speaking about her condition and raising concerns about bleeding linked to an earlier surgical procedure. The authorities have not publicly commented on her health.
## Background

Ogala was remanded in custody in Lagos in late October after being arraigned before a Federal High Court on three counts linked to a complaint by the cleric Pastor Chris Okafor. The charges relate to the alleged publication of photographs, alleged false electronic messages and alleged threats. She has not been convicted of anything, and has described the case as an attempt to stop her governorship bid. At a later sitting she apologised to the court for her conduct at an earlier hearing, and the judge fixed Friday, 6 November, for a ruling on her bail application. Earlier this week, a medical report shared online said she had been treated in June for severe anaemia linked to a fibroid condition.
## How people reacted
Fans and supporters have expressed concern and called for her release on health grounds, urging the authorities to make sure she receives proper medical care while the case continues.
## What happens next
Attention is now on the court's decision on her bail application.
more: Ogala reportedly blacked out and was bleeding.
She has been in custody since late October.
Her bail ruling was due on Friday.

stories.h: Davido prays for Zlatan and his wife at their white wedding in Morocco
stories.p: A video of Davido standing up to pray for Zlatan Ibile and his bride at their white wedding reception in Morocco has gone viral, surprising many fans amid VeryDarkMan's feud with both singers.
body: Davido has drawn attention online after a video showed him praying for Zlatan Ibile and his wife at their white wedding reception in Morocco.
## What happened

In footage shared on Friday, 6 November 2026, the singer is seen standing in a grand ballroom decorated with chandeliers and draped fabric, addressing the couple and their guests. Instead of giving a conventional speech, he said prayer was his priority. He began by mentioning the couple's traditional wedding, which had already taken place in Lagos, and said it had gone smoothly despite the large crowd, before praying for the newlyweds and their marriage.
## Background

Zlatan, one of Nigeria's best-known rappers, held his white wedding in Morocco after a traditional ceremony in Lagos. Videos from the celebrations have been widely shared, including one of Zlatan in tears and another of Davido singing along to Zlatan's song 'Inferno'. The weddings came during a public feud between Davido and social media activist VeryDarkMan (VDM), who has also taken swipes at Zlatan and said this week he would be turning his attention to the rapper. Davido's aide Israel DMW has also denied claims linking the singer to VDM's past arrest.
## How people reacted

Many fans praised Davido's sincerity and said the clip showed a spiritual side of him that people rarely see. Some asked why others were surprised, pointing out that he often speaks about his faith, while VDM's supporters continued to debate the feud in the comments.
more: Davido prayed for the couple at the Morocco reception.
Their traditional wedding took place in Lagos.
The video comes amid VDM's feud with both singers.

stories.h: Scripted slap from Sola Sobowale reportedly leaves mark on Toyin Abraham's face
stories.p: A behind-the-scenes clip shows Toyin Abraham being comforted on a film set after a scripted slap from veteran actress Sola Sobowale reportedly left a mark on her cheek. Toyin is said to have insisted on retaking the scene.
body: A behind-the-scenes video from a film set has got fans talking after a scripted slap from Sola Sobowale reportedly left a visible mark on Toyin Abraham's face.
## What the video shows

The clip, which went viral on Friday, 6 November 2026, shows Toyin seated and visibly shaken, with people around her fanning her and a man standing close by, apparently trying to reassure her. The scene appears to have been filmed indoors, in a home setting. According to reports, the slap was part of the script, but the impact was strong enough to leave a mark on her cheek. Toyin reportedly insisted that the crew retake the scene rather than stop filming for the day. The title of the production and the location of the shoot were not revealed.
## Background

Sola Sobowale is one of Nollywood's most celebrated veteran actresses, known for powerful performances over several decades, including her role in the 'King of Boys' films. This week she opened an elderly care home in Ibadan, which was commissioned by Governor Seyi Makinde. Toyin Abraham is a popular actress and producer who recently announced that veteran actor Pete Edochie will star in her December cinema film, 'Bestie'. She has also been in the news this week after sending a cease and desist letter to bloggers and announcing a change to her name.
## How people reacted

Fans praised Toyin's dedication to her craft, while others expressed concern for her and debated whether real slaps should be used in films at all, with some urging producers to use safer stage-fighting techniques.
more: The slap was reportedly scripted.
It reportedly left a mark on Toyin's cheek.
Toyin is said to have insisted on a retake.

stories.h: Kate Henshaw slams power minister Joseph Tegbe over electricity crisis
stories.p: Actress Kate Henshaw has criticised Minister of Power Joseph Tegbe in an Instagram video, complaining that power in her area lasts only minutes and mocking a reported remark about Nigerians asking for less electricity.
body: Veteran Nollywood actress Kate Henshaw has joined the growing number of Nigerians complaining about poor electricity supply, in a video aimed at the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe.
## What she said

In the video, posted on Instagram and reported on Friday, 6 November 2026, Henshaw said electricity in her area comes on for only a few minutes before going off again. She was particularly angered by a reported statement from the minister suggesting that some Nigerians had asked for power supply to be reduced because their freezers were freezing food. She accused officials of not telling the truth, demanded accountability for the billions of naira spent on the power sector, and mocked the way households now have to combine generators, inverters and solar panels to get through the day. She also criticised the minister's predecessor over repeated tariff increases. Henshaw said she had deliberately avoided commenting on national issues for most of the year, but had reached her limit.
## Background

Consumers in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo states have reported renewed outages this week. The minister has blamed the drop in supply on gas shortages, maintenance problems and reduced generation from hydropower plants. Comedian The Cute Abiola also posted videos this week appealing to President Bola Tinubu over the outages and economic hardship.
## How people reacted
The video drew thousands of comments from Nigerians who said they shared her frustration. The minister had not publicly responded to her comments at the time of writing.
more: Henshaw says power in her area lasts only minutes.
She demanded accountability for spending on the sector.
Outages have hit several states this week.

stories.h: Magixx says he struggled to pay bills after signing to Mavin Records
stories.p: Mavin singer Magixx says it took two to three months before he started earning after signing his record deal, and that people assumed he was rich. He says Nigerian artistes need songs with international appeal to build real wealth.
body: Mavin Records singer Magixx has spoken about the financial realities of the music business, saying a record deal does not automatically make an artiste rich.
## What he said

Speaking on an episode of a music podcast, reported on Friday, 6 November 2026, the singer said he did not start earning from music immediately after signing to Don Jazzy's label. It took about two to three months before money began to come in, he said, and during that time he struggled to pay bills and meet family responsibilities. He added that asking people for help became difficult because they assumed his record deal meant he was already wealthy, while he was also expected to keep up the image of a star, including wearing expensive designer clothes.
## Building wealth
Magixx said Nigerian musicians need songs with international appeal to make serious money, and that releasing hits consistently is key to staying financially stable.
## Background

Magixx signed with Mavin Records in 2021 and is known for songs such as 'Love Don't Cost a Dime'. His comments come in the same week that fellow Mavin artiste Crayon posted, and later deleted, emotional messages about the label and his friendship with Rema.
## How people reacted
Fans thanked him for being honest about the pressures young artistes face, while some said his story showed why upcoming musicians should manage expectations after signing a deal.
more: Magixx says it took months before he started earning.
He says people assumed he was rich.
He wants Nigerian artistes to aim for global hits.

stories.h: Newcastle defender Amar Dedic stopped by armed police over bow and arrows
stories.p: Police in Northumberland stopped Newcastle United defender Amar Dedic and took a bow and arrows from his car after a member of the public reported two men carrying the weapon near a reservoir. Officers concluded there was no threat.
body: Newcastle United defender Amar Dedic was stopped by police in north-east England after a member of the public reported seeing two men carrying a bow and arrows.
## What happened

According to reports on Friday, 6 November 2026, the 24-year-old Bosnia-Herzegovina international was travelling in a car with a friend when the report was made about two men walking along a track near a reservoir off Military Road in the Harlow Hill area of Northumberland. Six patrol cars, including armed officers, were reportedly sent, and the car was stopped about seven miles from where the men had been seen. Northumbria Police said that after speaking to the men they concluded there was no threat to the public, and a bow and arrows were seized from the vehicle. The police statement did not name the player.
## Teammates arrive

Dedic reportedly cooperated fully with officers and had no bad intentions. Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett reportedly arrived while officers were still talking to him, having been in the area, and stopped to support him.
## Background
Dedic is a full-back who has played for clubs including Red Bull Salzburg and Benfica before moving to Newcastle.
more: Armed officers stopped Dedic's car in Northumberland.
A bow and arrows were seized.
Police said there was no threat to the public.

stories.h: Kenneth Okonkwo predicts Atiku will be on 2027 ballot, claims NDC faces bigger problems than ADC
stories.p: Nollywood actor and politician Kenneth Okonkwo says the NDC is facing more serious problems than the ADC, and insists Atiku Abubakar will be on the ballot in 2027. He spoke days after a Federal High Court ruling nullified the emergence of the ADC's national chairman.
body: Nigeria's opposition politics is getting more interesting as the battle for relevance ahead of the 2027 general elections continues.
## What Okonkwo said
Veteran Nollywood actor and politician Kenneth Okonkwo has stirred another round of debate after claiming that the NDC is facing more serious problems than the African Democratic Congress (ADC).
According to Okonkwo, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar will still be on the ballot in the 2027 presidential election.
"NDC is facing more problems than ADC. Atiku Abubakar will be on the ballot," he said.
## An interesting twist

Okonkwo is making this prediction at a time when the leadership of his own party, the ADC, is facing a major legal setback after a Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the emergence of its national chairman and the actions taken under his leadership.
That raises an obvious question. If his own party is battling a leadership crisis in court, how certain can anyone be about what will happen to other opposition parties before 2027?
## Politics full of surprises

Nigerian politics has a way of surprising even those who believe they understand the game. Alliances can change overnight, party leaders can fall out, and court judgments can completely change the direction of an election.

For Atiku, who has contested the presidency several times, whether he will appear on the ballot again remains a major subject of discussion. Okonkwo's prediction should be understood as his political opinion rather than confirmation of Atiku's candidacy.
As 2027 approaches, Nigerians are watching closely to see whether opposition politicians will eventually unite behind a common candidate or continue to pursue separate presidential ambitions.
## Over to you

Why is Kenneth Okonkwo so confident about Atiku's political future when his own party is struggling with a leadership crisis? Is he seeing something other Nigerians have not noticed, or is this another round of political calculation ahead of 2027?
more: Okonkwo says the NDC has bigger problems than the ADC.
He insists Atiku will be on the 2027 ballot.
A court recently nullified the ADC chairman's emergence.

stories.h: Wike mocks Peter Obi: 'Vote for him as president of social media, not Nigeria'
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has told Rivers voters that Peter Obi is popular on social media but lacks the capacity to lead Nigeria, also mocking the NDC candidate's habit of carrying his own bag. Obi's supporters hit back online.
body: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has taken another swipe at Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).
## What Wike said

Speaking at a town hall meeting in Abonnema, Akuku-Toru Local Government Area of Rivers State, on Thursday, 5 November 2026, Wike reportedly said that people who wanted a president of social media should vote for Obi, but that he should not be voted for as president of Nigeria. He also mocked Obi's well-known habit of carrying his own bag, saying it did not show that he had the capacity to rule the country.
## Background

Wike, a former Rivers governor, leads the Rainbow Coalition, a group of PDP and other politicians backing President Bola Tinubu's re-election in the presidential election scheduled for 16 January 2027. He has repeatedly criticised Obi in recent weeks. Obi, a former Anambra governor, has a large following among young voters, especially online, and is running with Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate. Wike made the comments during a busy week in which he also spoke about Governor Siminalayi Fubara's political future and denied any role in the court ruling on the Imo West Senate ticket.
## How people reacted

Obi's supporters responded angrily online, with many saying Wike could not campaign without mentioning Obi and describing the former governor's simple lifestyle as a strength. Supporters of the minister said Obi's online popularity had not translated into votes in Rivers State in the past. Obi's campaign had not publicly responded to the latest remarks at the time of writing.
more: Wike spoke at a town hall in Abonnema, Rivers State.
He mocked Obi for carrying his own bag.
Obi's supporters hit back online.

stories.h: Cute Abiola says he sold one of his cars as he appeals to Tinubu over power and hardship
stories.p: Comedian and skit maker The Cute Abiola has posted videos appealing to President Tinubu over poor electricity and the cost of living, saying his solar system had run down and that he recently sold one of his cars to settle debts.
body: Comedian and skit maker The Cute Abiola has joined Nigerians complaining about poor electricity supply and economic hardship, in videos addressed directly to President Bola Tinubu.
## What he said

In one video shared online on Friday, 6 November 2026, the content creator said his solar power system had gone off because of heavy use during the long power outages in his area. He appealed to the President to help Nigerians, saying everywhere was hot, there was no light and the suffering was too much. In another video, he said he had just sold one of his cars to ease his financial situation, explaining that he owed people money and still needed funds to shoot new content. He added that he hoped things would not get to the point where he had to sell his house.
## Background

Abiola, whose real name is Abdulgafar Ahmed, became popular for his comedy skits and is a former member of the Nigerian Navy. His complaints come as consumers in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo states report renewed power outages, which the federal government has blamed on gas shortages, maintenance problems and reduced hydropower generation. The government has also started paying a ₦50,000 monthly relief grant to selected households.
## How people reacted

Many fans sympathised and said his videos reflected what millions of Nigerians are going through. Some critics said he had not praised the government when things were going well for him and was now blaming the President, while others said public figures should be free to speak about their struggles.
more: Cute Abiola says his solar system has run down.
He says he sold one of his cars to settle debts.
Outages have hit several states this week.

stories.h: Nigerians rally around Mrs Gertrude Anulika Ngwu after humiliating incident at husband's Ozo title-taking ceremony
stories.p: Well-wishers have been visiting Mrs Gertrude Anulika Ngwu with gifts, money and encouragement after a viral video showed her co-wife's children refusing to spray money on her at her husband's Ozo title ceremony. Her story has reopened a conversation about how childless women are treated in some Nigerian families.
body: What was supposed to be a day of celebration has turned into a story of humiliation, public sympathy and unexpected kindness for Mrs Gertrude Anulika Ngwu, whose experience at her husband's Ozo title-taking ceremony has drawn wide attention on social media.

Kind-hearted Nigerians have continued to visit her, offering financial help, gifts and words of encouragement after a viral video showed her being treated in a way many viewers described as humiliating.
## The viral video

The video captured an uncomfortable moment during the traditional ceremony when the children of her husband's second wife reportedly refused to spray money on her, despite repeated appeals from the master of ceremonies.
According to accounts shared alongside the footage, the children had earlier sprayed money on their biological mother. When the MC encouraged them to do the same for Mrs Anulika, they declined.

For many Nigerians who watched, it was a painful scene: a woman attending an important ceremony in her husband's life, yet appearing to be left out of a celebration in which she should have felt included and respected.
## Years of mockery
The story became even more emotional following claims that Mrs Anulika had endured years of mockery over her inability to have children.

Reports online suggest she eventually moved back to her father's home after allegedly facing repeated ridicule from her co-wife and the woman's children. These allegations have not been independently verified.
## Strangers show her love
Nigerians who were touched by her story have decided to show her some love. In recent days, well-wishers have visited her at her father's residence with gifts, financial support and encouragement.

Some supporters have donated hundreds of thousands of naira, while others bought her a new mobile phone. More visits are planned: one support group has announced a grand visit to her village in Ukeh, Enugu State, on Friday, 6 November 2026, with supporters from Anambra, Imo and Abia invited to meet at Ekochin Bus Stop, 9th Mile.

Perhaps that is the most touching part of this story. People who have never met Mrs Anulika are going out of their way to make her smile. Strangers who watched a few minutes of her experience online have become concerned about her welfare.
## A conversation about childlessness
Her story has also reopened an important conversation about how women who struggle with childlessness are treated in some Nigerian families.

Why should a woman's value in marriage be measured by the number of children she has? Why should a woman who has spent years in a marriage be made to feel less important simply because she has not given birth?
Marriage comes with its own difficulties, but no woman deserves to be publicly ridiculed or denied basic respect because of her circumstances.
## Compassion still lives

Whatever may have happened behind the scenes in this family, the incident has clearly touched a nerve. The growing support for Mrs Anulika shows that compassion still has a place in society. Even at a time when many people are struggling financially, some are willing to share what little they have to comfort someone they believe has been treated unfairly.

One can only hope the support continues beyond social media and that she finds lasting peace, dignity and happiness. To every Nigerian who has visited, donated or offered her a kind word, your gesture deserves recognition. Sometimes, all a person needs is to know that somebody cares.
## Over to you

Should a woman who has no biological children be treated differently in her husband's family, especially when he marries another wife who has children? What happened to compassion, fairness and respect in our traditional family system?
more: Her co-wife's children reportedly refused to spray money on her.
Well-wishers have donated money, gifts and a new phone.
A support group is visiting her village in Ukeh, Enugu State.

stories.h: Power outages hit Lagos, Abuja and three other states as government blames gas shortages
stories.p: Residents of Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo are facing worsening power cuts. Power Minister Joseph Tegbe has reportedly blamed gas shortages, maintenance work and low water levels at hydro plants, saying there has been no national grid collapse.
body: Electricity consumers in Lagos, Abuja, Ogun, Kwara and Oyo states are facing renewed power outages, prompting the federal government to explain the situation.
## What the minister said

Minister of Power Joseph Tegbe reportedly blamed the drop in supply on gas shortages, maintenance problems and reduced generation from hydropower plants because of low water levels, according to reports on Thursday, 5 November 2026. The government said there had been no major collapse of the national grid. It also said it had cleared 44 containers of equipment that had been stranded at the ports, which are needed to improve supply.
## Impact on customers

The outages have caused particular anger among Band A customers, who pay the highest tariffs in return for at least 20 hours of electricity a day. Ikeja Electric this week issued seven apologies in nine days for failing to meet that promise. Many households and businesses have had to spend more on fuel for generators.
## Public frustration

The outages have drawn complaints from well-known Nigerians. On Friday, comedian The Cute Abiola posted a video addressed to President Bola Tinubu, saying his solar system had run down after days of poor supply, that everywhere was hot and that the suffering was too much.
Actress Kate Henshaw also posted a video criticising the minister, saying power in her area lasts only minutes before going off and demanding accountability for spending on the sector.
## Grid operator explains

In a statement on Thursday, 5 November, the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), which manages the national grid, blamed the drop in supply on inadequate gas deliveries to thermal power plants and lower water levels at hydroelectric stations. It said this had forced it to cut the power allocated to distribution companies, leading to more load shedding, and that the impact varies from one region to another.
## Minister gives timeline

In a further statement on Friday, 6 November, Minister of Power Joseph Tegbe said three problems had combined to cut supply: planned maintenance at the Egbin power station, limited gas supply to some thermal plants, and sabotage of key transmission lines, which he said had been especially damaging in Lagos because it blocked routes engineers would normally use to redirect power. He said damaged generating units would be brought back in phases, with the first expected back within 48 to 72 hours, and that work was under way with gas suppliers and on repairs. Singer Spyro also said on Saturday that when he visited an Eko Electricity Distribution Company office to complain, he found staff fanning themselves because of the heat.
## Background

Nigeria's electricity supply has long been unreliable, with generation often far below demand for a population of more than 200 million. Gas supply problems, vandalism of pipelines and weak transmission infrastructure are frequent causes. The government says it is working to expand generation and transmission capacity, while critics, including opposition candidates, say progress has been too slow. Electricity is expected to be a major issue in the 2027 campaign.
## What happens next
Consumers are waiting for a clear timeline from the government and distribution companies on when supply will improve.

stories.h: Tension erupts as angry crowd throws stones towards stage while Nasarawa governor addresses presidential campaign rally
stories.p: A presidential campaign rally was disrupted when some angry youths in the crowd reportedly threw stones towards the stage as Nasarawa State Governor Abdullahi Sule addressed supporters. Photos show stones lying on the stage beside the governor and his team.
body: What was supposed to be a peaceful political campaign reportedly took a dramatic turn when some angry youths in the crowd began throwing stones towards the stage while Nasarawa State Governor Abdullahi Sule was addressing supporters.
## What happened
The incident happened during a presidential campaign rally on Thursday, 5 November 2026, and created tension at the venue as the gathering was disrupted.

Photos from the event show large stones lying on the red carpet of the stage, close to the governor's feet. In one image, a man in a suit bends to pick up one of the stones as the governor, microphone in hand, points towards the crowd, with security officers standing beside him.
## Why the anger?

The exact reason for the crowd's anger remains unclear. The incident does, however, raise questions about growing frustration among sections of the population and how political leaders are being received at public gatherings.
For many Nigerians struggling with the rising cost of living, unemployment and insecurity, political promises are becoming harder to accept without visible results.
Even so, it would be premature to blame those grievances for the disturbance without hearing from the people involved.
## Violence is never the answer

Whatever the reason, throwing stones at a political gathering is dangerous and should never be encouraged. People have every right to express their dissatisfaction with their leaders, but political disagreement should never turn violent.
## Over to you
Are Nigerian politicians beginning to face the anger and frustration of the people they have been making promises to for years?
more: Stones were thrown towards the stage during the governor's speech.
The reason for the crowd's anger is unclear.
Photos show stones on the stage near the governor.

stories.h: "I would have been worried if Amaechi stood a chance in Rivers State": Wike fires back at political rivals
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has dismissed Rotimi Amaechi's chances in Rivers State, insisting he remains a major force there even though he is no longer governor. He also claimed the APC barely existed in Rivers before he backed it, and that he has "killed the Obi wave" in the FCT.
body: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has once again spoken boldly about his political influence in Rivers State, dismissing the chances of former Minister of Transportation Rotimi Amaechi and insisting he remains a major force in the state.
## "You cannot wish me away"
According to Wike, he would only have reason to worry if Amaechi stood a realistic chance of a significant political comeback in Rivers State.
The former Rivers governor made it clear that leaving Government House in Port Harcourt has not reduced his influence or weakened the structures he built over the years.
"I am not a governor, I am a minister, but you cannot wish me away in Rivers State, because the people know what I stand for and because of the people I have raised," Wike said.
His statement appears to be a direct message to those who believe his appointment as FCT Minister has taken him away from the centre of Rivers politics.
## Claims about the APC
Wike also claimed that the All Progressives Congress (APC) had little political strength in Rivers State before he decided to support the party.
"Before I decided to support the APC, the party did not exist in Rivers State," he said.
That is a bold claim, given the long rivalry between Wike and Amaechi, who both served as governors of Rivers State at different times.
## "I have killed the Obi wave"
Wike did not limit his remarks to Rivers. He also turned his attention to the movement around NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi, claiming he had already weakened its influence in the FCT.
"As for the NDC, I have killed the Obi wave in the FCT," he said.
The remarks reflect Wike's confidence in his political strength, although his claims about the APC and about Obi's support remain his own assessment.
## The road to 2027

With the 2027 general elections approaching, the political battle in Rivers State is expected to draw even more attention. Wike, Amaechi and other influential figures may once again find themselves on opposing sides as parties prepare for another contest.
For now, Wike is making one thing clear to his opponents: he may no longer be governor, but he has no intention of surrendering his influence in Rivers State.
## Over to you
Is Wike still as politically powerful in Rivers State as he believes, or will the 2027 elections reveal a different picture?

stories.h: "If not for VeryDarkMan, I wouldn't be where I am today": Ratel Princess Jojooflele expresses gratitude from China
stories.p: Social media personality Jojooflele, known as the Ratel Princess, has publicly thanked VeryDarkMan for changing her life, saying her following and opportunities grew after she met him. She spoke from China, a long way from the Nedu controversy that first brought her into the spotlight.
body: Popular social media personality Jojooflele, widely known as the Ratel Princess, has openly expressed her appreciation for VeryDarkMan (VDM), acknowledging the role he has played in changing her life.
## "If not for VDM"
Speaking from China, Jojooflele reflected on how far she has come and how her association with VDM opened doors she probably never imagined would open so soon.
"If not for VDM, I wouldn't be where I am today," she said.

According to her, things took a completely different turn after she met VeryDarkMan. Her social media pages began attracting more attention, her followers increased, and opportunities started coming her way.
## How it all started

What makes her story even more interesting is how it began. Many will remember the controversy involving Nedu, when Jojooflele found herself at the centre of public attention, with people discussing her personal life and questioning her actions.
For someone else, that kind of controversy could have been enough to damage their confidence or push them off social media completely.

Instead, Jojooflele turned the attention into something positive. Rather than letting the controversy define her future, she kept building her presence online and eventually became a familiar face among supporters of the Ratel Movement.
## A lesson in gratitude
Today, she is in China, reflecting on her journey and publicly appreciating someone she believes contributed greatly to her success.
Jojooflele deserves credit for how she has handled her growing popularity. The right connections can open doors, but what you do with those opportunities matters just as much.

Her appreciation for VDM is also worth acknowledging. In a society where people sometimes forget those who supported them once they start to succeed, publicly recognising someone's contribution says a lot about gratitude.
## Setbacks are not the end

Perhaps the biggest lesson here is never to be too quick to conclude that your present difficulties will decide your future. The situation people expect to destroy you can end up introducing you to opportunities you never knew existed.
What looks like a setback today may become part of the story you proudly tell tomorrow.
## Over to you
What do you think about Jojooflele's journey from the Nedu controversy to her growing popularity and opportunities abroad?

stories.h: "My oga had nothing to do with any plot to arrest VeryDarkMan": Israel DMW defends Davido amid controversy
stories.p: Davido's aide Israel DMW has denied that the singer had any hand in an alleged plot to have VeryDarkMan arrested, or in Naira Marley's troubles during the Mohbad case. He says those who told VDM otherwise lied.
body: Davido's loyal aide, Israel DMW, has come out to defend his boss following speculation linking the Afrobeats superstar to an alleged plot to get social media activist VeryDarkMan (VDM) arrested.
## "Oga had no hands in it"
In a post addressed to "Dearest Nigerians", Israel said Davido had no hand in Naira Marley's ordeal during the Mohbad case, nor in any plot to see VDM arrested.
He said those who were in the WhatsApp group linked to the matter got there without Davido's instructions or approval, and that those who told VDM otherwise "fully lied".
## Sam Klef, Mohbad's catalogue and Zino
Israel also asked why Davido would have any issue with Sam Klef, and denied that the singer ever asked for Mohbad's music catalogue or tried to sign Zino.
## "Naira and oga are cool"

According to Israel, there was serious pressure on Davido at the time to unfollow Naira Marley on Instagram, but he categorically refused, saying he wanted the police to do their job and did not want to act on hearsay.
"Naira and oga are cool," he wrote, adding that the two even made a hit song together.
On an incident at Naira Marley's house, Israel said it involved Tolu 30BG, who had a disagreement with one of Naira's boys, and insisted that nobody was beaten or attacked.
## Why the denial matters

VDM is known for speaking openly about controversial issues and challenging influential people, which has earned him both strong supporters and fierce critics. Whenever the names Davido and VeryDarkMan appear in the same controversy, Nigerians are bound to have plenty to say.
Israel's message is straightforward: whatever controversy surrounds VDM, his boss should not be accused of involvement without proof.
It is important to note that the allegations remain unverified. Israel's denial is his own position, and there is no established evidence that Davido took part in any plot to have VDM arrested.
## Over to you

Who is actually behind the alleged move to arrest VeryDarkMan, and why is Davido's name being mentioned? Until credible evidence emerges, the public should be careful about turning social media speculation into fact.
